_comment: Windows 11 dark. Every number here is Microsoft's unless its line says otherwise. Sources: microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml controls/dev/CommonStyles/*_themeresources.xaml for the control metrics, CommunityToolkit/Windows components/SettingsControls for the settings card, and the Fluent 2 geometry page for the two corner radii. Where nothing is published -- the taskbar has no public design documentation at all -- the number is ours and is called out below.
_bar: OURS: the taskbar is shell chrome and Microsoft documents none of it. 48 is the measured height at 100% scaling; 8 and 4 are read off screenshots.
_groups: SettingsCardSpacing 4 and SettingsCardPadding 16 are verbatim from the Community Toolkit sample the official docs point at. cardRadius is OverlayCornerRadius, the 8 that Windows gives windows, flyouts and dialogs.
_notifications: A toast and a card in the notification centre are the same component in two expand states. 16 is the standard flyout padding, 8 the overlay radius, 40 the app-icon box.
_popout: The Quick Settings flyout. OURS, measured from screenshots; Microsoft publishes nothing for it.
_rail: NavigationView ships OpenPaneLength = 320.0 and the Settings app does not override it. 16 is the pane's own horizontal inset, NavigationViewAutoSuggestBoxMargin. Both of these are tokens only because this theme asked for them: the facade used to declare 210 and 10 on itself.
_type: 600 is Semibold. Windows 11's typography rules say Semibold for emphasis and never Bold, so this is the heaviest weight the theme ever asks for.
_corners: 0 because Windows rounds WINDOWS, not the screen. This is what makes CornerWedge the empty implementation the interface explicitly supports -- the four ScreenCorner windows still exist, reserve nothing and take no input.
_motion: ControlFastAnimationDuration. WinUI ships exactly three durations -- 83, 167, 250 -- and one easing spline, ControlFastOutSlowInKeySpline = 0,0,0,1. Note that hover is NOT among the things that animate: Windows swaps the brush on a DiscreteObjectKeyFrame at time zero.
